description: Captured issues #890–#903 for declared-dependency parity (#905). #900 includes the historical multi-ref Depends on: #899, #662 (in-set #899, external #662).

issues.body:
## Problem

Agent Pipeline has a durable per-item advance controller and a durable multi-item loop, but it has no restart-safe factory lifecycle spanning intake, contract adoption, loop execution, later merge/release phases, and engine promotion. The current factory plan assigns that repository-level lifecycle to an outer agent, which would duplicate Pipeline's scheduler and make chat/session state part of execution authority.

## Required outcome

Add a disabled-by-default Pipeline-owned macro-controller that adopts immutable execution-contract revisions and reconciles them against live GitHub, git, configuration, and durable run state. The controller defines the coarse factory phase and next deterministic action while delegating all item scheduling, stage progression, and recovery to the existing durable loop/advance controllers.

The contract must capture, at minimum:

- repository/base identity and observed base SHA;
- selector, issue/PR identities, milestones, and dependency edges;
- linked durable loop/run identities;
- controller identity and revision;
- outer-host identity separately from implementer/reviewer treatments;
- authority-policy, engine-pin, configuration, and treatment fingerprints;
- current coarse phase, completion policy, and next action.

A replan creates a retained new revision with its live-state reason; it never overwrites an accepted contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The macro-controller is off by default and does not change existing interactive `pipeline`, `single`, `loop`, merge, or release behavior when disabled.
- [ ] Starting/resuming uses one Pipeline-owned contract, ledger/run namespace, lock, and action history; no outer host, Hermes database, or agent chat becomes a second authoritative scheduler or store.
- [ ] A contract revision is immutable, canonically hashed, and records all minimum identities/fingerprints above.
- [ ] The service controller, outer host, implementer, reviewer, and privileged mutation actor are represented as distinct identities; a non-Claude controller is never silently recorded as Codex.
- [ ] The current controller revision is monotonic and exposed to read-only consumers.
- [ ] Adoption/replan uses compare-and-set; a stale expected revision or changed live identity fails without partial mutation.
- [ ] Duplicate/concurrent ticks dispatch any coarse action at most once.
- [ ] Restart reconstructs phase and next action from durable evidence plus freshly observed external truth, never conversation memory.
- [ ] The controller delegates whole items to the native loop and cannot invoke a per-stage transition.
- [ ] Default active-item behavior remains one; any existing explicit concurrency policy and proven-independence rules remain authoritative rather than being widened by this controller.
- [ ] Tests inject GitHub/git/clock/service seams and cover crash before claim, after claim, after child start, after ambiguous child result, replan, stale revision, duplicate tick, and legacy run identity.
- [ ] Run evidence and documentation explain which controller/revision owned every coarse action.
- [ ] `node scripts/build.mjs` and `npm run ci` pass with generated mirrors current.

## Non-goals

- Implementing autonomous merge, release finalization, engine installation, or Hermes integration.
- Replacing the existing dependency/ownership scheduler or recovery controller.
- Granting authority from labels, prompts, profiles, or outer-host identity.
- Creating a distributed/multi-host lock from current host-local PID semantics.

## Related foundations

- #784 — outer-host lifecycle identity and registry.
- #530 / the living independent-scheduler specs — dependency/ownership scheduling.
- #761 — production recovery-controller integration.
- #662 — separate shadow-qualification requirement before any autonomous merge executor.
issues.title: feat(factory): add a durable macro-controller and immutable execution-contract revisions

issues.body:
Depends on: #890

## Problem

Factory state is currently split across per-issue JSON status, loop audit/status, controller process records, run artifacts, provider state, engine pinning, and service-manager state. An operator or external supervisor cannot obtain one authoritative snapshot, and the raw loop projection cannot be exposed remotely because it includes lock/supervisor bearer tokens and unbounded internal evidence.

The current supervisor heartbeat is refreshed around completed cycles. A long blocking dispatch can therefore look stale even when its process is live, while a future provider cooldown may be legitimate waiting rather than a wedge.

## Required outcome

Add `pipeline factory status --json` plus human-readable output as a pure, versioned, allowlisted read model over #890's controller and existing durable evidence. Add controller-owned heartbeat/operation evidence sufficient to distinguish process liveness, durable progress, and expected waiting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pipeline factory status --json` writes exactly one unfenced versioned JSON object, including structured error/degraded states.
- [ ] Status performs no GitHub, git, service, control, ledger, event, or run-artifact mutation.
- [ ] The snapshot includes controller/service identity, mode/revision, active contract/run, engine/treatment/authority fingerprints, active/queued/held counts, per-item coarse state and stage, linked advance run/PR/candidate, current operation/deadline, last durable progress, expected wait/deadline, provider cooldown, next action, lock/liveness projection, event/write-health, and actual/estimated/unknown cost coverage.
- [ ] Remote output is assembled from an explicit allowlist; raw lock/supervisor records, bearer tokens, credentials, secret references, process environments, prompts/tool output, local auth material, and unsanitized issue/comment/reason text never appear.
- [ ] Tests inject canary secrets and prompt-like issue/reason text into every source object and prove no canary or raw instruction appears in JSON, prose, or error output.
- [ ] A controller-owned heartbeat advances on a bounded independent cadence during long item dispatches, waits, and recovery backoff without requiring model/worker progress messages.
- [ ] Heartbeat refresh stops after lock loss/terminal exit and failed persistence is visible rather than reported healthy.
- [ ] Health represents process liveness, durable workflow progress, and expected waiting independently.
- [ ] `suspected_stuck` requires fresh controller liveness plus an explicitly started operation past its deadline with no durable progress.
- [ ] `dead` requires stale heartbeat plus same-host process/service absence proof; cross-host or insufficient evidence is `unknown`.
- [ ] CI/provider/backoff/dependency/capacity/human waiting before a recorded deadline is healthy waiting, not stuck.
- [ ] Missing telemetry and cost remain unknown; no remaining-quota percentage or zero-cost inference is emitted.
- [ ] Legacy runs and missing optional sources remain readable with explicit unknown/legacy attribution.
- [ ] Unit tests use injected clocks, process probes, stores, status readers, and no real network/git/subprocess calls.
- [ ] Generated CLI/config/host docs and `plugin/` mirror remain current; `npm run ci` passes.

## Non-goals

- A dashboard, notification system, or mutating command.
- Exposing the raw loop-store status object over HTTP/MCP.
- Replacing run artifacts, per-issue status, audit, logs, or scoreboard.
- Claiming cross-host process death from host-local evidence.

## Related

- #154 and #155 shipped per-issue JSON status and stable run/event surfaces.
- #301 shipped historical factory scoreboard reporting.
- #398 addressed indefinite harness termination but not factory health projection.
- #654 requests campaign-specific progress and must not become the generic factory health owner.
issues.title: feat(factory): add aggregate status and independent controller health

issues.body:
Depends on: #890, #891

Coordinates with: #823, #840

## Problem

Factory progress is split across macro-controller evidence, durable-loop events, linked per-item advance events, and optional advance-only event sinks. Consumers must currently understand several storage formats and lifecycle quirks. They cannot reconnect from a stable cursor, and the living follow/notification contracts disagree about whether successful `loop_run_complete` is terminal. Stable run-artifact manifests also lag newer write-health, supervisor, and action-evidence files.

## Required outcome

Add `pipeline factory watch --jsonl` as a read-only, replayable projection over the canonical controller, loop, and linked advance streams. Extend the configurable event-sink contract to loop/controller events without changing the raw evidence or making delivery execution-gating.

The command must support at least `--from <cursor>`, `--follow`, `--material`, and `--until-terminal`. Each projected record needs a versioned source identity, source position, deterministic event identity, factory/run/item correlation, observed time, event time when available, kind, and an allowlisted payload.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A consumer can start from the beginning, reconnect from a returned cursor, and observe every retained event at least once without silent gaps.
- [ ] Duplicate delivery is detectable by deterministic event identity; ordering is stable within each source and the join never claims a false global causal order.
- [ ] Truncation, rotation, malformed records, missing linked streams, retention gaps, and legacy records are surfaced as typed records/degraded state rather than skipped silently.
- [ ] `loop_run_complete` and `loop_run_stopped` are both terminal across loop follow, material notification, outer-host reattach, and `--until-terminal` behavior.
- [ ] A `loop_item_advance_linked` record causes the watcher to follow the canonical linked advance stream, including stage/review/gate/blocker events, without relying on polling each item independently.
- [ ] `--material` reuses the host-neutral material-event policy and remains observational; notification or sink failure never gates execution.
- [ ] Loop/controller sink delivery preserves the byte-identical serialized source record and per-source order while retaining existing `additive` versus `exclusive` semantics.
- [ ] Existing per-advance sink behavior remains compatible; no network delivery is added to a ledger critical section.
- [ ] Stable artifact manifests/specs include all currently promised controller, supervisor, action-evidence, event, and write-health artifacts, with explicit legacy compatibility.
- [ ] The remote projection is allowlisted and redacted; lock/supervisor tokens, credentials, raw prompts/tool output, and unsanitized external text do not escape.
- [ ] Tests cover replay, reconnect, duplicate records, partial trailing lines, file replacement/truncation, linked streams, both terminal kinds, sink failure, slow additive sinks, and secret canaries.
- [ ] `node scripts/build.mjs` and `npm run ci` pass with generated mirrors and docs current.

## Non-goals

- Persisting notification acknowledgements or implementing alert policy; that belongs to the observer issue.
- Making an external event sink authoritative for factory state.
- Replacing raw run artifacts or the historical scoreboard.
- Stretching host-local lock/liveness guarantees across machines.

## Related foundations

- #611, #666, #667 — durable loop follow and linked progress foundations.
- #742 — host-neutral material progress notification.
- #823 — incremental single-poller advance event reads.
- #840 — asynchronous additive event-sink delivery.
- #503 — fleet telemetry design/spec foundation; shipped no runtime exporter.
issues.title: feat(factory): add a unified replayable factory watch and loop event export

issues.body:
Depends on: #891, #892

Coordinates with: #742, #840

## Problem

Agent Pipeline records rich run evidence, but there is no restart-safe observer that turns it into bounded operator notifications and proves that monitoring itself is alive. A Hermes session, dashboard connection, or best-effort notification cannot safely be the cursor, acknowledgement store, or source of workflow truth. Without durable replay and separate delivery health, reconnects can silently drop or duplicate progress, and an unhealthy monitor can be mistaken for a healthy factory.

## Required outcome

Add a deterministic, read-only factory observer that consumes #892's replayable watch, persists consumer cursors and an idempotent notification outbox outside authoritative run directories, emits a bounded material-progress feed, and publishes an independent dead-man heartbeat. The observer reports controller liveness, durable workflow progress, and legitimate expected waiting as separate dimensions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The observer never writes controller contracts, ledgers, locks, item state, GitHub labels/comments, merge state, or canonical run evidence.
- [ ] Each configured consumer has a durable versioned cursor and outbox; restart/reconnect replays retained events at least once and downstream deduplication uses stable event/notification identities.
- [ ] Cursor advancement cannot acknowledge an event before its notification has either been durably queued or explicitly suppressed by versioned policy.
- [ ] Material policy covers factory/run start and terminal state, item admission, stage/round changes, PR/candidate changes, review/gate/blocker state, expected cooldown/hold, operator request, merge/release/upgrade milestones, stuck suspicion, degraded evidence, and delivery failure.
- [ ] Repeated unchanged states are coalesced; an ongoing run emits only a bounded configurable heartbeat and state-change alerts.
- [ ] The observer distinguishes fresh controller heartbeat, last durable progress, and an expected-wait deadline. Expected CI/provider/dependency/human waits before deadline do not generate stuck alerts.
- [ ] Stuck/dead/recovered alerts have stable lifecycle identities and do not flap on every poll.
- [ ] Notification delivery status is separate from source event-write health and factory health; delivery failure is observable but never authorizes, blocks, or advances execution.
- [ ] An external dead-man target can detect that the observer stopped reporting even when Hermes and Pipeline share a host.
- [ ] Consumer payloads use #892's redacted DTO only; raw event files, bearer tokens, credentials, prompts/tool output, and unsanitized external text are not forwarded.
- [ ] Tests inject clocks, crash points, duplicate events, provider waits, long dispatches, cursor corruption, unavailable destinations, and secret canaries without real network or subprocess calls.
- [ ] Operator docs include an on-demand drill-down path to raw local evidence without putting that evidence in notifications.
- [ ] `node scripts/build.mjs` and `npm run ci` pass with generated mirrors and docs current.

## Non-goals

- A Hermes-specific dashboard or messaging implementation.
- Using notification acknowledgements as workflow authority.
- Replacing `pipeline scoreboard`, audit, status, or raw logs.
- Guaranteeing exactly-once external delivery.

## Related foundations

- #742 — host-neutral material progress notification.
- #503 — fleet telemetry design/spec foundation.
- #301 — historical factory scoreboard.
- #840 — asynchronous additive event delivery.

## Buzz delivery clarification

Buzz is the selected first production destination, but this issue remains transport-neutral. The native Hermes/Buzz implementation belongs to #897 and live deployment belongs to #898; this issue owns the observer/outbox contract they consume.

### Additional acceptance criteria

- [ ] A destination adapter returns a typed accepted, rejected, or unknown receipt containing destination identity, stable notification identity, safe external receipt id when available, and observation time.
- [ ] The observer marks an outbox item delivered only after confirmed destination acceptance; timeout or unknown delivery leaves it pending or reconciles by stable identity.
- [ ] Notification formatting and publication are deterministic and redacted and do not invoke a Hermes/model reasoning turn.
- [ ] For Buzz, a returned Nostr event id is delivery evidence only; it does not prove operator read, acknowledge an alert, or mutate Pipeline state.
- [ ] Buzz/relay/network failure is reported separately from controller and source health, leaves notifications retryable, and never gates execution.
- [ ] The external dead-man destination remains independent of both Buzz on services and Hermes/agent-box so that the primary delivery path cannot hide its own outage.
issues.title: feat(factory): add a durable observer, material alerts, and dead-man heartbeat

issues.body:
Depends on: #890, #891

Related: #510, #647

## Problem

The factory plan needs remote/operator control, but current control is split among process signals, loop/item behavior, human-request answers, and direct service-manager commands. Exposing those primitives to Hermes would grant too much authority and make retries, concurrent operator turns, and stale views unsafe.

## Required outcome

Add a narrow Pipeline-owned factory control surface for `pause`, `drain`, `resume`, `answer`, and `stop`. Every command uses a versioned typed envelope with command id, actor identity, expected controller revision, requested operation, bounded arguments, and observed result. Commands must be idempotent and compare-and-set against current durable state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CLI commands and an embeddable service seam share one control implementation; neither caller edits run files, labels, locks, or service state directly.
- [ ] Repeating a command id returns the retained original result without repeating side effects; reusing an id with different arguments fails.
- [ ] A stale expected revision, wrong repository/run identity, terminal run, or policy mismatch fails closed with current safe status and no partial mutation.
- [ ] `pause` prevents new dispatch/admission at a durable safe boundary while preserving active work and records who/why/revision.
- [ ] `drain` prevents new dispatch/admission, lets already active work reach a defined safe boundary, and reaches a durable drained state that survives restart.
- [ ] `resume` requires disabled/pause/drain state plus lock, authority/config/engine fingerprints, and live-state preflight to match; it cannot revive a terminal or superseded run implicitly.
- [ ] `answer` targets exactly one outstanding typed human request from #647, validates its schema/revision, and cannot be interpreted as generic shell, merge, label, or policy authority.
- [ ] `stop` first commits a durable disabled/stop intent that prevents restart, then performs bounded cancellation/cleanup; process termination before durable disablement is rejected.
- [ ] Concurrent Hermes/CLI/system turns serialize through the controller and cannot dispatch or answer twice.
- [ ] Actor identity is audit attribution only; paired chat identity does not imply merge, release, or engine-install authority.
- [ ] The surface exposes no arbitrary shell, raw `gh`, direct per-stage transition, label mutation, merge/release/tag/install verb, credential, or lock token.
- [ ] Tests cover duplicate commands, stale revisions, race with tick/terminal transition, crash at every durable boundary, long-running drain, outstanding human requests, and restart reconciliation.
- [ ] Existing interactive commands and item-level pause semantics remain compatible when the factory controller is disabled.
- [ ] Generated CLI/config/host docs and `plugin/` mirror remain current; `npm run ci` passes.

## Non-goals

- Autonomous merge/release/install operations.
- Treating the outer host or messaging platform as an authority source.
- Replacing the current whole-item loop execution contract.
- A generic remote shell or service-manager proxy.

## Authenticated transport-origin clarification

Remote controls need immutable transport provenance in addition to a resolved actor label. This keeps signed Buzz attribution outside model control while remaining adapter-neutral.

### Additional acceptance criteria

- [ ] The command envelope includes an authenticated immutable origin with adapter, principal, conversation/channel id, and message/event id, stamped by the trusted adapter from transport context.
- [ ] Model arguments, display names, reactions, pairing, and channel membership cannot supply or override command origin.
- [ ] The adapter deterministically derives or binds a stable command identity from the authenticated message event and typed operation; replay of the same event cannot repeat a mutation.
- [ ] The retained command decision links immutable origin, resolved actor, command id, target run/revision, and result without exposing transport secrets.
- [ ] Signed transport identity is audit attribution only and does not imply merge, release, install, policy, or stage authority.
issues.title: feat(factory): add revision-checked idempotent pause, drain, resume, answer, and stop

issues.body:
Depends on: #890, #891

## Problem

Provider quota exhaustion, rate limiting, authentication failures, transient outages, and harness-local cooldowns can currently surface as generic item failures or repeated retries. A factory controller needs to stop spending attempts against a known-unavailable provider while continuing independent work, without guessing quota percentages or asking an outer agent to infer recovery from prose.

## Required outcome

Add a durable provider-scoped availability/circuit-breaker ledger and typed classification contract. Controller scheduling consumes this state to defer only work whose next required treatment depends on the unavailable provider, records an evidence-backed `not_before`, performs bounded probes when appropriate, and resumes the exact held stage after recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Availability keys include provider plus credential/account/config identity without storing or exposing secret material.
- [ ] Only an explicit allowlist of typed adapter/harness signals can open or extend a breaker; unstructured model text and generic nonzero exits cannot.
- [ ] State distinguishes at least rate/quota limit, authentication/configuration failure, provider outage, local harness failure, and unknown failure.
- [ ] Each transition records source evidence reference, first/last observation, attempt count, next permitted probe/dispatch time, and deterministic backoff policy version.
- [ ] A breaker suppresses only stages that require that provider; provider-independent reconciliation, monitoring, review, or other configured providers may continue.
- [ ] Deferred items retain their exact issue/run/stage/round identity and resume through the normal Pipeline controller rather than a special bypass.
- [ ] Successful typed use/probe closes or relaxes a breaker; authentication/configuration failures require an explicit configuration change or operator action rather than infinite probes.
- [ ] Restart preserves cooldown/deadline state and duplicate concurrent failures converge idempotently.
- [ ] Status/watch/observer projections expose provider, class, evidence time, `not_before`, affected work count, and unknowns without tokens, headers, raw responses, or invented remaining-quota percentages.
- [ ] Expected waiting before `not_before` is healthy wait, not stuck; a missed post-deadline probe/action becomes visible.
- [ ] Tests cover mixed Grok/Codex work, concurrent failures, retry-after parsing, clock skew, restart, credential/config change, unknown errors, and redaction canaries.
- [ ] Existing adapter retry behavior remains compatible unless the factory controller explicitly consumes the new typed state.
- [ ] Generated docs and `plugin/` mirror remain current; `npm run ci` passes.

## Non-goals

- Forecasting provider spend or remaining quota from incomplete telemetry.
- Allowing Hermes/model prose to set cooldown state directly.
- Replacing bounded stage/item retry budgets.
- Multi-account load balancing or credential rotation.
issues.title: feat(factory): add provider-scoped availability circuit breakers and cooldown ledger

issues.body:
Depends on: #890, #894

Related: #766

## Problem

The proposed factory needs a reachable intake path, but a newly filed issue must not become executable merely because a form, label, or outer agent says it is ready. There is no durable provenance/admission contract connecting operator intent, Hermes planning proposals, dependency discovery, and an immutable Pipeline execution-contract revision.

## Required outcome

Add a repository Issue Form and Pipeline-owned intake/admission workflow. The form captures operator intent and constraints into a stable provenance block and places the issue in a non-executable backlog state. Hermes or another planner may submit a typed admission/decomposition proposal, but only the factory controller validates current GitHub truth and adopts it through a revision-checked contract update.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Issue Form captures objective, background, constraints/non-goals, acceptance evidence, risk/authority class, dependency hints, target milestone/priority, and optional operator contact without secrets.
- [ ] Created issues carry a stable machine-readable provenance marker and enter `pipeline:backlog` (or an equivalent non-executable state), never a ready/active stage.
- [ ] Replayed form/webhook/import processing is idempotent and cannot duplicate provenance or admission actions.
- [ ] A planner proposal has a versioned schema with source issue SHA/update identity, proposed scope, dependency edges, milestones, priority, risk, treatments, and rationale references.
- [ ] Admission validates issue openness, repository identity, current body/update identity, dependency references, existing Pipeline ownership/state, policy/config/engine fingerprints, and expected controller revision.
- [ ] Stale, malformed, duplicate, circular, cross-repository, already-owned, or policy-incompatible proposals fail with typed reasons and no partial labels/comments/contract mutation.
- [ ] Accepted admission creates a new immutable #890 contract revision and only then performs any derived Pipeline state transition through existing stage-authority paths.
- [ ] Planner/Hermes identity is attribution, not authority; untrusted issue text cannot request shell, merge, release, tag, credential, policy, or direct stage operations.
- [ ] Proposed decomposition remains compatible with #766 and does not duplicate its child-issue implementation.
- [ ] Operator edits after proposal either trigger explicit revalidation/replan or rejection; they are never silently ignored.
- [ ] Tests cover duplicate delivery, stale issue edits, invalid/cyclic dependencies, prompt-like body content, concurrent admissions, partial GitHub failure, and restart reconciliation using injected GitHub/controller seams.
- [ ] Generated forms/docs and `plugin/` mirror remain current; `npm run ci` passes.

## Non-goals

- A general-purpose backlog product or replacement for GitHub Issues.
- Letting Hermes create executable state without deterministic validation.
- Implementing epic decomposition itself; coordinate with #766.
- Automatic merge, release, deployment, or engine installation.

## Messaging-provenance clarification

A Hermes proposal may originate from Buzz, but messaging identity is provenance rather than admission authority.

### Additional acceptance criteria

- [ ] A planner proposal may retain authenticated transport provenance with adapter, signed principal, conversation/channel id, message/event id, and the corresponding Hermes session/proposal identity.
- [ ] Re-delivery of the same authenticated event/proposal identity is idempotent and cannot duplicate intake, decomposition, issue creation, or contract adoption.
- [ ] Model-provided display names or origin fields cannot override trusted adapter provenance.
- [ ] A signed Buzz event, allowlisted operator, channel membership, or message receipt remains attribution only; current GitHub truth and the revision-checked Pipeline admission contract remain authoritative.
- [ ] Raw messaging credentials, private keys, unbounded chat history, and unrelated channel content are never copied into issue provenance or execution contracts.
issues.title: feat(intake): add factory Issue Form provenance and revision-checked backlog admission

issues.body:
Depends on #891.
Depends on #892.
Depends on #894.
Depends on #907.

Builds on: #784

## Problem

Hermes Agent can provide the persistent conversation and messaging access missing from the factory plan, but Agent Pipeline has no first-class Hermes outer-host package or constrained factory tool profile. Treating Hermes delegation/Kanban/chat memory as the run controller would create a second scheduler and ledger; giving it shell or GitHub credentials would bypass Pipeline authority.

## Required outcome

Add a manifest-driven `hermes` outer host and a least-privilege factory operator profile. Hermes may start or reattach to a durable Pipeline run, read the redacted factory status/watch/log surfaces, submit typed #894 control commands, and propose intake/contract revisions. Agent Pipeline remains the sole controller, scheduler, ledger, recovery authority, and evidence source.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PIPELINE_OUTER_HOST=hermes` is discovered through the existing public manifest/registry seam without shared-code `if host === hermes` lifecycle branches.
- [ ] The host implements invocation, flushed handoff parsing, event follow, material notification, reattach, nonterminal wait cancellation, terminal handling, cleanup, and final summary according to #784 conformance.
- [ ] A cancelled/interrupted Hermes wait is never reported as Pipeline completion; reattach uses durable run identity and current status rather than conversation memory.
- [ ] Hermes exposes only versioned typed tools for factory status/watch/log drill-down, pause/drain/resume/answer/stop, and admission/contract proposals.
- [ ] Tool schemas require repository/run identity, command id, and expected revision where mutating; responses preserve Pipeline error/degraded states.
- [ ] No Hermes tool exposes arbitrary shell, filesystem paths outside safe display references, raw `gh`, label/stage mutation, merge/release/tag/install operations, lock/supervisor tokens, credentials, prompts/tool output, or raw internal status objects.
- [ ] Hermes Kanban, delegation records, cron state, sessions, and memory are explicitly non-authoritative and cannot be mapped to Pipeline item ownership or retry state.
- [ ] Hermes/Gateway restart and complete Hermes outage do not kill or pause the Pipeline controller; after recovery, missed material events replay from the durable observer cursor.
- [ ] Outer-host identity remains distinct from controller, Grok implementer, Codex reviewer, and privileged mutation actor in status/evidence.
- [ ] The profile works with an allowlisted messaging identity and a private dashboard, but paired chat identity grants no merge/release/install authority.
- [ ] Host package, manifest schema, install/uninstall, doctor, notify-surface behavior, and lifecycle conformance have hermetic tests with injected processes/HTTP.
- [ ] Existing Claude/Grok/Codex/stdout hosts remain behaviorally unchanged.
- [ ] Generated host docs and `plugin/` mirror remain current; `npm run ci` passes.

## Non-goals

- Installing or operating the Hermes service on agent-box.
- Using Hermes as the per-item/stage executor; the existing `agent-system` executor role is orthogonal.
- Making Hermes a scheduler, run store, service manager, credential broker, merge executor, or monitoring source of truth.
- Adding autonomous merge/release/install policy.

## Related foundations

- #784 — manifest-driven outer-host lifecycle and identity.
- #314 — Hermes as a stage executor; this issue is the separate outer-host/operator role.
- #742 — host-neutral material progress notifications.

## Native Buzz operator-access scope

The initial production messaging adapter is Hermes v2026.8.3's native Buzz gateway, connected outbound from agent-box to the existing Buzz relay on services. Buzz remains replaceable and the Pipeline protocol remains channel-neutral. Buzz Desktop and buzz-acp are not the selected production path because the native gateway preserves the constrained Hermes profile/session and supports a per-platform MCP allowlist.

### Additional acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Buzz platform uses a dedicated Hermes Nostr identity and normal private factory stream, exact watched/home channel and operator-public-key allowlists, allow-all disabled, and mention-required behavior.
- [ ] The effective Buzz platform toolset exposes exactly one factory MCP server and only tools allowed by the current promotion level; terminal, filesystem, browser, generic web, delegation, GitHub, configuration, skill installation, and self-update including /update are structurally unavailable.
- [ ] A live tool-catalog negative test proves forbidden capabilities are absent rather than relying on prompt instructions.
- [ ] The adapter stamps signed author public key, channel/conversation id, and Nostr event id as immutable #894 origin. Model arguments, display names, reactions, pairing, and membership cannot supply or override attribution.
- [ ] A stable Pipeline command id is deterministically bound to the inbound Buzz event and typed operation, so reconnect/backfill/replay returns the retained result without a second mutation.
- [ ] A command is represented as accepted only after a threaded response returns Pipeline's command id and resulting/current controller revision.
- [ ] Full-gateway downtime cannot silently lose an accepted command: bounded durable inbound backfill replays by event id, or a missing receipt is explicitly unaccepted and requires retry of the same intent.
- [ ] Material observer notifications publish deterministically from #893's observer-owned Buzz destination under a distinct scoped publisher identity, without a Hermes/model turn; the returned Buzz event id is retained only as delivery evidence and failed delivery leaves the outbox pending.
- [ ] The dedicated Buzz private key is unavailable to model prompts/results, factory tools, child MCP environments, logs, environment dumps, and repository config; the operator private key is never installed on agent-box.
- [ ] Buzz or Hermes outage does not pause, complete, retry, or authorize Pipeline, and the external dead-man remains outside Buzz.
- [ ] Hosting or changing the Buzz relay on services is out of scope; #898 owns deployment compatibility and live calibration against the existing service.

## Generic MCP package boundary

#907 owns the independently installable, host-neutral MCP-to-CLI server, version/capability handshake, generic profiles, structured Pipeline result forwarding, and forbidden-tool conformance. This issue consumes that package and owns only the Hermes outer-host lifecycle plus Buzz-specific identity, profile selection, allowlisting, receipts, restart, and deployment behavior.

### Additional acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Hermes profile installs/configures #907's published MCP artifact rather than maintaining a second Hermes-specific mapping of Pipeline commands.
- [ ] Hermes/Buzz configuration selects only #907's required read-only or factory-control profile and cannot widen the generic package configuration from conversation.
- [ ] Generic MCP behavior is tested in #907's host-neutral conformance suite; this issue adds only Hermes/Buzz integration and lifecycle tests.
issues.title: feat(outer-host): add Hermes Agent, native Buzz access, and narrow factory tools

issues.body:
## Goal

Deploy one scoped autonomous Agent Pipeline factory on `agent-box`. Mitchell controls and monitors the factory from the private Buzz stream `pipeline-factory`.

Hermes is the outer supervisor. Hermes invokes the installed Agent Pipeline CLI. Pipeline remains the development state machine and owns each issue run. Grok 4.5 performs planning, implementation, and fixes. Codex performs review.

The pilot must complete one approved release grant without approval for each pull request. It must implement each issue in order, merge the exact eligible pull request, prove that the merge is in `main`, prepare and merge the release pull request, verify the release, install that exact release on `agent-box`, and use the installed release for the next release.

## Startup configuration

- [ ] Use Hermes v0.20.0 from tag `v2026.8.3` and the native Buzz gateway.
- [ ] Use Buzz CLI v0.5.2 at commit `3e48f1b2365d326ee1c9582448d86a99b44ecd5d`.
- [ ] Use provider `xai-oauth` and model `grok-4.5` for Hermes and all Pipeline Grok roles. Configure no Grok fallback. Stop if this provider cannot run `grok-4.5`.
- [ ] Use the existing `mcomardo` account for the pilot. Record that this account and its GitHub token are broad authority, not a least-privilege boundary.
- [ ] Fix the Tailscale split-DNS rule that makes `buzz.accidentalhedgefund.com` return `SERVFAIL`. Do not use an IP URL or `/etc/hosts`.
- [ ] Use one dedicated Hermes Nostr identity. Permit only Mitchell's exact signed operator public key. Require a mention. Keep the stream private and without expiry.
- [ ] Use `/home/mcomardo/dev/agent-pipeline` as the working directory.
- [ ] Invoke `/usr/bin/node /home/mcomardo/.codex/skills/pipeline/scripts/pipeline.mjs`. Do not invoke the stale `/usr/local/bin/pipeline` launcher.
- [ ] Set an explicit service `PATH` that contains `/home/mcomardo/.local/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin`, and `/bin`.
- [ ] Keep the current v1.31.1 production pin for the first pilot run. Use the clean v1.32.0 `main` checkout as the v1.33.0 code base. Do not promote v1.32.0 because its FRG notes disclose test-only overrides. Store `AGENT_PIPELINE_PRODUCTION_PIN` outside the checkout.
- [ ] Run `pipeline doctor --json --harness-smoke` in the exact systemd environment before admission.

## Authority contract

Accept a factory grant only after the native Buzz gateway filters Mitchell's exact operator key and private stream. The same-user wrapper validates the relay-observed sender, channel, message, thread, and time fields, but it does not independently verify the Nostr signature. The grant must name the repository, base branch, milestone, frozen issue order, exact release version, allowed issue-pull-request merges, allowed release-pull-request merge, engine promotion, and a seven-day expiry.

Use this first grant:

> Run Agent Pipeline release v1.33.0 from `main` for issues #905, #874, and #870, in that order. You may merge their exact eligible pull requests, prepare and merge the exact release pull request, verify publication, and promote and install v1.33.0. Stop on scope drift or failed evidence.

The grant does not authorize another repository, issue, pull request, head commit, base branch, release version, tag, credential, policy, force push, hard reset, or arbitrary shell action.

## Delivery cycle

For each issue, fetch the current `origin/main`, run `pipeline single <issue> --profile codex` in its own transient user-systemd unit, and retain the flushed run identity. Wait for `pipeline:ready-to-deploy`. Resolve and merge only the exact linked eligible pull request. Query GitHub again, record `mergeCommit.oid`, fetch `main`, and require the `origin/main` tip to equal that merge result for this frozen first train. Stop if another commit advanced the base. Fast-forward the control checkout. Start the next issue only after this proof passes.

Do not use the current milestone loop for this pilot. Its ready-to-deploy completion rule does not prove integration before dependent work starts.

After all three issue merges:

- [ ] Fetch `main`, record the exact final integrated commit, and create or verify a clean run-confined checkout at that commit. Keep this candidate identity separate from the deployed #898 wrapper commit.
- [ ] Create a fresh `factory-gate-v1` candidate pack for v1.33.0. Do not reuse #749 or #750.
- [ ] Use the two fresh issue runs for live item, throughput, taxonomy, pull-request, check, and OpenSpec proof. For fault classes that have no safe CLI injection seam, run only the closed manifest list of exact candidate-commit-bound Layer A probes. Label those proofs `layer_a`; do not report them as live injections. This v1.33.0-only exception expires into #908.
- [ ] Do not accept a caller-authored pass, status, metric, receipt, invented observation, or open-soak waiver.
- [ ] Supply the FRG attestation key through a systemd credential. Do not put it in prompts, logs, environment dumps, or the repository.
- [ ] Run `pipeline factory-gate --for 1.33.0 --from-run <run-id> --observations <file>` and stop on any missing, failed, stale, or provenance-mismatched proof. Require the producer HMAC to bind the final candidate commit, manifest, exact loop, issue set, and proof digests.
- [ ] Prepare the release from the exact clean candidate checkout with `pipeline release 1.33.0 --no-edit --theme "Scoped factory and loop correctness"`.
- [ ] Add the immutable and latest FRG evidence to the release branch. Wait for all checks on the resulting exact head.
- [ ] Verify the release pull request's repository, base, branch, title, version files, changed-file allowlist, FRG identity, exact head, and green checks.
- [ ] Merge only that exact release head. On timeout or an ambiguous response, inspect GitHub state before any retry.
- [ ] Prove that `v1.33.0` is an annotated tag whose peeled commit is the release merge commit. Verify a published, non-draft GitHub Release.
- [ ] Drain Pipeline units. Fast-forward the checkout to released `main`. Promote the production pin and install the exact `v1.33.0` tag.
- [ ] Run `pipeline doctor --json --harness-smoke`. Prove that the pin, install receipt, installed version, tag, and release commit agree.
- [ ] If installation or validation fails, restore and reinstall the previous exact pin, run doctor, and keep the factory stopped.
- [ ] Record the installed engine version in the terminal Buzz report. Admit the next release only after all checks pass.

## Process and monitoring

Run Hermes as a persistent user-systemd service with `Restart=on-failure`. Run each Pipeline process in a separate transient unit with `KillMode=control-group`. A Hermes restart must not stop an active Pipeline run.

Use one small host-local watcher. Send material Pipeline transitions and one heartbeat after 15 minutes without a material event to one Buzz thread for each run. Do not send raw event records, prompts, model output, environment values, or secrets. Pipeline must continue if Buzz or the watcher fails.

Store only the minimum restart record under `~/.local/state/hermes-factory/`: active grant fingerprint, run identity, systemd unit, current exact target, and last reported event cursor. This record is not a second Pipeline ledger.

## Stop conditions

Stop the factory and report the exact evidence when the signed grant is absent, expired, or mismatched; a target or head drifts; a required check or FRG scenario fails; merge or publication state is ambiguous; the installed version does not match the verified release; or rollback cannot be proved.

## Non-goals

- A public MCP server, typed factory API, dashboard, or new Pipeline telemetry.
- A second scheduler, controller, or lifecycle ledger.
- General machine-selected merge authority outside an exact signed release grant.
- Distributed locking or general fleet management.
- Productizing the pilot service topology for other hosts.
issues.title: ops(factory): deploy a scoped autonomous Hermes/Buzz factory on agent-box

issues.body:
Depends on: #890, #894

Related: #590, #618, #662, #842

## Problem

A prompt or machine-local policy file cannot structurally prevent a worker or outer host from bypassing Pipeline if that process inherits an operator home, broad GitHub credential, or executable `gh` path. Current harness children inherit the parent environment/HOME, and the repository already recognizes same-UID isolation limits. Unattended privileged actions therefore require a separately privileged authority boundary before any merge/release/install executor is safe.

## Required outcome

Add a machine-scoped authority-policy format and a privilege-separated action broker/service. The broker alone holds narrowly scoped mutation credentials and implements a fixed allowlist of typed operations. Pipeline submits canonically signed/fingerprinted action requests with live evidence references; Hermes, Grok/Codex workers, general harnesses, and the unprivileged controller cannot read the credentials or invoke raw mutation primitives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Policy is versioned, canonically fingerprinted, disabled by default, names repository/base, allowed operation classes, caller/service identities, risk limits, evidence requirements, expiry, and revocation state.
- [ ] Policy activation/rotation/revocation is an explicit operator action outside model or label control; revocation wins over queued/in-flight requests at every pre-commit check.
- [ ] The broker runs under a distinct OS/service identity and receives only operation-specific credentials; unprivileged Pipeline, Hermes, and worker environments contain no broker token, raw GitHub mutation credential, operator home, SSH signing key, release token, or install privilege.
- [ ] The interface is a closed versioned schema, not arbitrary shell/argv/URL/GraphQL/REST forwarding, and rejects unknown fields/operations.
- [ ] Every request includes stable action id, repository/base/candidate identities, exact expected SHAs/refs, controller contract/revision, authority fingerprint, evidence digests, caller identity, and expiry.
- [ ] Requests are idempotent; duplicate action ids return retained results, conflicting reuse fails, and ambiguous external outcomes reconcile before any retry.
- [ ] The broker re-fetches required live truth immediately before mutation and fails closed on drift, stale evidence, missing qualification, policy mismatch, unavailable provider, or unverifiable identity.
- [ ] Broker audit evidence records request/result identities and safe reason codes without credentials, headers, raw prompts/tool output, or secret-bearing command lines.
- [ ] Live integration proof demonstrates Hermes and Grok/Codex worker processes cannot merge/push protected base, create tags/releases, install packages, read broker credentials, or call the broker outside their allowlist.
- [ ] Compromise/revocation tests cover broker unavailable, token rotation, stale queued request, process crash before/after external mutation, duplicate delivery, tampered evidence, and operator emergency stop.
- [ ] Existing interactive operator merge/release behavior remains unchanged until a later operation-specific service explicitly adopts the broker.
- [ ] Security/operator docs define containment limits, credential scopes, incident shutdown, audit export, and why same-UID policy alone is insufficient.
- [ ] `node scripts/build.mjs` and `npm run ci` pass; any privileged integration test is isolated and opt-in with a safe fixture repository.

## Non-goals

- Implementing merge, release, tag, or engine-install business logic in this issue.
- Treating a paired chat identity, label, prompt, outer-host profile, or contract as sufficient authority.
- Solving arbitrary multi-host/distributed trust.
- Passing operator credentials through Hermes or worker environments.
issues.title: feat(factory): add machine-scoped authority policy and a privilege-separated action broker

issues.body:
Depends on: #899, #662

## Problem

All authorized merges need one exact-head, idempotent mutation path. However, an ordinary issue pull request, a release pull request, and an engine-promotion pull request do not have the same evidence. The current issue text applies ordinary issue-stage and qualification fields to every caller. That can reject a valid release or promotion, or encourage a special caller to bypass the shared merge implementation.

## Required outcome

Converge all supported callers on one exact-head merge service. Apply one common mechanical safety envelope, then validate a typed evidence profile for the caller and pull-request purpose. A caller cannot borrow or omit evidence from another profile.

## Evidence profiles

- `operator_issue`: session-bound operator authority, exact issue and pull request, current Pipeline stage, reviewed head, and ordinary merge eligibility.
- `scoped_factory_issue`: current signed release grant, in-scope issue and order, exact linked pull request and reviewed head, current `pipeline:ready-to-deploy` evidence, and current base proof.
- `qualified_factory_issue`: current #662 qualification, #306 eligibility, #899 authority fingerprint, risk allowance, controller revision, and stable action identity.
- `scoped_factory_release`: current signed release grant, exact version and release pull request, release-managed changed-file allowlist, current FRG attestation, exact release head, and required checks.
- `scoped_factory_engine_promotion`: current signed release grant, verified tag and peeled release commit, current and target production-pin identities, drained-state evidence, exact promotion head, and rollback target.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every request declares a supported caller class and pull-request purpose. The service does not infer them from a title, branch name, label, prompt, model, or Hermes identity.
- [ ] Every profile uses the same fresh checks for repository, base, pull-request number, exact expected head, mergeability, conflicts, draft state, required checks, required reviews, unresolved conversations, and base drift.
- [ ] Each profile validates only its defined authority and evidence fields. Ordinary issue-stage evidence cannot replace release or promotion evidence, and release or promotion evidence cannot authorize an ordinary issue merge.
- [ ] General qualified-machine issue merges remain disabled until #662 qualification and #899 authority are current for the exact policy boundary.
- [ ] A scoped factory request is valid only inside an explicit repository policy that permits the named signed-grant profile. Expired, revoked, mismatched, or broadened grants fail closed.
- [ ] High-risk, policy-excluded, exception-bearing, unknown, or qualification-boundary-mismatched ordinary candidates remain operator-owned unless the active profile explicitly permits the exact action.
- [ ] Immediately before mutation, the service refreshes all common and profile-specific evidence and stops on any drift.
- [ ] Merge uses the exact expected head. A changed head or base requires fresh evidence and authority.
- [ ] Stable action identities make duplicate requests idempotent. A timeout or ambiguous response is reconciled against current pull-request and base truth before any retry.
- [ ] Revocation, disable, or stop wins through the last pre-commit boundary. Post-merge evidence records the exact merge result and base identity without secrets.
- [ ] Stage import and reconciliation use existing transition authority. External merge evidence does not authorize an unrelated stage change.
- [ ] Tests cover every profile, cross-profile evidence substitution, missing fields, stale grants, stale qualification, policy changes, high risk, head and base drift, conflicts, changed checks or reviews, duplicate requests, ambiguous merge, revocation races, and secret canaries.
- [ ] Generated docs, OpenSpec text, and the `plugin/` mirror remain current. `npm run ci` passes.

## Non-goals

- Treating every `pipeline:ready-to-deploy` candidate as autonomously mergeable.
- Weakening #662 for the general qualified-machine profile.
- Implementing scheduling, FRG execution, release finalization, engine installation, or deployment.
- Adding a broad `auto_merge` switch.

## Related work

#306 owns deterministic ordinary merge eligibility. #662 owns empirical qualification for general machine-selected issue merges. #899 owns the hardened machine authority broker. #902 owns release finalization. #903 owns engine promotion.
issues.title: feat(merge): converge operator and qualified-machine callers on one exact-head merge service

issues.body:
## Summary

Dependent milestone work must not start merely because its prerequisite reached ready-to-deploy. This change adds an operator-compatible integrated completion policy that waits for a verified merge result to appear in the configured base before releasing dependents. It provides the durable, restart-safe frontier needed by supervised Hermes operation without performing a merge or granting an agent additional authority.

## User story

As an operator running a dependent milestone,
I want each dependent issue to start from a base that contains its prerequisite,
so that serial scheduling also represents serial integration rather than a sequence of unrelated branches.

As an operator supervising the factory through Hermes,
I want ready-to-deploy candidates awaiting my merge to appear as healthy, durable waits,
so that I can intervene without the controller declaring a deadlock, losing progress, or relying on chat memory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Run contracts support explicit ready or merged completion policies, preserve ready as the compatibility default, and expose the immutable selected policy in status and audit evidence.
- [ ] One policy-aware completion rule governs dependency release, scheduling eligibility, deadlock detection, concurrency accounting, terminal completion, status, and reporting.
- [ ] Under merged completion, ready-to-deploy is a nonterminal waiting state and never satisfies an in-run dependency.
- [ ] Under merged completion, a same-repository external prerequisite is not satisfied by issue closure or a merged flag alone; it requires current integration proof for the configured base.
- [ ] Waiting for an operator merge or for base visibility is reported as a healthy expected wait with an actionable reason and deadline behavior, not as no progress or dependency deadlock.
- [ ] With completion capacity one, an uncontained ready-to-deploy candidate continues to consume that capacity; higher explicit concurrency may admit only siblings already proven independent by existing scheduling rules.
- [ ] Integration evidence binds the exact reviewed pull-request head to the same merged pull request and records the merge-method-specific result, target base, observed base-at-merge identity, current fetched base identity, observation times, and containment result.
- [ ] For a squash merge, the resulting merge commit—not the reviewed branch head—is the object required to be contained in the current base.
- [ ] A dependent is released only after a fresh authoritative base observation proves that the bound merge result is contained in the configured base.
- [ ] A wrong or superseded head, wrong base, missing merge result, stale or unavailable base observation, unrelated base advancement, or unverifiable pull-request identity fails closed without releasing dependents.
- [ ] Observing a qualifying merge durably establishes the integration barrier before any dependent can start; the barrier clears only after verified containment and emits auditable set and clear evidence.
- [ ] Before dependent dispatch, its effective worktree base is proven to include the contained integration result; a stale pre-existing worktree is refreshed safely or remains held.
- [ ] Restart reconstructs ready-waiting, merge-observed, containment-pending, contained, held, and terminal frontier states from durable evidence plus fresh external truth without duplicating transitions.
- [ ] Ready-only runs preserve their current stop-at-ready behavior and perform no merge request or additional privileged action.
- [ ] Tests cover ready compatibility, manual squash merge, merge-commit and rebase outcomes where supported, changed head, changed base, missing result identity, merge observed before base visibility, stale dependent worktree, source unavailability, restart at every frontier state, duplicate ticks, and dependency release timing.
- [ ] Generated documentation and packaged mirrors are current, and the repository's full CI command passes.

## Out of scope

- Requesting or performing a machine merge; #906 owns qualified factory merge actions.
- Defining merge eligibility, empirical qualification, authority policy, or credential isolation; #662, #899, and #900 own those concerns.
- Release, tag, deployment, or engine-promotion finalization.
- Expanding default concurrency or replacing the existing dependency and ownership scheduler.

## Background

Depends on #905.

This issue originally combined two concerns: an authority-neutral completion and base-containment frontier, and submission of qualified machine merge requests through #900. Those concerns are now separated so supervised operation with an explicit human merge can become dependency-safe before autonomous merge qualification is available. Issue #906 adds the later machine-request path on top of this frontier.

The previous requirement that the exact reviewed candidate commit itself be an ancestor of the base was incompatible with Pipeline's normal squash merge. The reviewed head identifies what was authorized; the pull request's merge result identifies what was integrated; containment of that result in a freshly observed base is the release proof.
issues.title: feat(loop): add operator-compatible integrated completion and a durable base frontier

issues.body:
## Dependencies

- #899
- #900
- #901
- #906

## Problem

`pipeline release` prepares a release PR and intentionally stops. Completing a milestone still requires exact release-PR validation, FRG/soak evidence, an authorized merge, workflow observation, annotated-tag verification, and published GitHub Release verification. An outer agent must not stitch these steps together from chat memory or retry an ambiguous merge/tag outcome destructively.

## Required outcome

Add an idempotent, restart-safe release finalizer that binds every checkpoint to one version, release PR, exact reviewed head, merge SHA, attested FRG result, soak-defect preflight, annotated tag, and published Release. Privileged mutation goes only through #899/#900; workflow/tag/Release observation remains read-only and evidence-backed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Finalization begins from an immutable request containing repository/base, semantic version, expected release branch/PR/head, milestone/controller revision, authority fingerprint, FRG evidence identity, and stable action id.
- [ ] It resolves exactly one open `release/vX.Y.Z` PR and validates expected title/base/branch, version files, generated mirror, ROADMAP entry, and an explicit bounded release-managed file set.
- [ ] It verifies current cryptographically attested FRG pass evidence for the exact version/head/policy and performs the open-soak-defect preflight; missing/unknown/stale/mismatched evidence fails closed without an invented waiver.
- [ ] Immediately before merge it requires non-draft, clean mergeability, exact unchanged head/base, current required checks/reviews/protection, and #900/#899 authorization.
- [ ] Merge is exact-head and idempotent. Timeout/ambiguous results reconcile PR and base containment before retry and never merge another head.
- [ ] After merge, the finalizer observes the designated tag workflow and proves `vX.Y.Z` is an annotated tag whose peeled commit equals the exact release merge SHA.
- [ ] It observes the release workflow and proves a published, non-draft, non-prerelease (unless explicitly requested) GitHub Release for that tag with non-empty notes and expected repository identity.
- [ ] A pre-existing mismatched/lightweight tag, wrong peeled SHA, draft/mismatched Release, multiple release PRs, or rewritten workflow evidence is a hard held failure; the finalizer never force-retags, deletes tags, or edits/replaces a conflicting Release.
- [ ] Durable checkpoints cover request accepted, PR validated, FRG/soak validated, merge requested/reconciled, tag observed/verified, Release observed/verified, and terminal outcome.
- [ ] Restart from every checkpoint re-observes live truth, repeats no completed mutation, and preserves stable action identities.
- [ ] Status/watch/observer surfaces expose safe milestone/version/checkpoint/expected wait/failure evidence without secrets or raw workflow logs.
- [ ] Operator disable/revocation wins through the last pre-merge boundary; post-merge observation may safely finish even if mutation authority is revoked.
- [ ] Tests cover exact success, each validation failure, ambiguous merge, delayed/failed workflows, wrong/lightweight tag, wrong/draft Release, duplicate ticks, crash at every checkpoint, and revocation race using injected GitHub/git/workflow seams.
- [ ] Existing release preparation and operator-only workflows remain unchanged unless the finalizer is explicitly invoked under accepted policy.
- [ ] Generated CLI/config/docs and `plugin/` mirror remain current; `npm run ci` passes.

## Non-goals

- Preparing arbitrary release contents outside the existing release workflow.
- Force-retagging, rewriting published releases, or bypassing FRG/soak evidence.
- Promoting/installing the production engine pin; that is a separate change.
- Granting authority from a milestone, tag name, Hermes identity, or model judgment.
issues.title: feat(release): add an exact-evidence idempotent release finalizer

issues.body:
Depends on: #894, #899, #902

Builds on: #762

## Problem

Production engine pinning identifies an approved release, but the factory has no coordinated, restart-safe path from a verified published release through pin promotion, drained agent-box installation, validation, resume, and proven rollback. Letting Hermes or a model run package-manager/shell commands would bypass authority and could change the engine while issues are active.

## Required outcome

Add an exact-tag engine promotion/install/validation/rollback workflow coordinated by the Pipeline macro-controller. Promotion is compare-and-set against #762's production pin; agent-box mutation is a fixed privileged #899 operation; the factory must be durably drained with no active issue before any installed-engine change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A promotion request binds repository, exact semantic version/tag, peeled release SHA, verified #902 finalization evidence, FRG identity, current/target pin revisions, controller revision, authority fingerprint, host identity, and stable action id.
- [ ] Pin promotion is an explicit generated change with exact version/tag/SHA/FRG evidence, full CI, exact-head authorized merge, and retained previous FRG-passed pin; it is not a direct model edit to protected state.
- [ ] Promotion and rollback use compare-and-set and are idempotent: replay of the same identity is a no-op, while conflicting current pin/tag/SHA/host state fails closed.
- [ ] Before installation, admissions and new dispatch are stopped, #894 reaches durable drained state, no item/advance operation is active, and the controller records the exact safe boundary.
- [ ] The privileged installer accepts only a pinned allowlisted install operation for the exact verified tag/SHA and cannot execute arbitrary shell/package arguments supplied by Hermes, models, issues, or prompts.
- [ ] Post-install validation proves CLI/package/version coherence, `pipeline doctor --json`, configuration/schema compatibility, controller/status/watch access, and role-aware Grok implementer plus Codex reviewer smoke tests.
- [ ] Resume occurs only after all validation evidence is durable and the installed version matches the promoted pin exactly.
- [ ] Any install/validation failure triggers a bounded rollback to the retained previous FRG-passed exact tag, reruns the same coherence/doctor/role smoke, and restores the prior pin through the controlled compare-and-set path.
- [ ] If rollback cannot be proven, the factory remains durably paused/disabled and emits a critical operator alert; it never resumes on an unknown or mismatched engine.
- [ ] Release tags and published Releases are observational inputs and are never rewritten during installation rollback.
- [ ] Crash/reboot at every checkpoint reconciles installed version, pin state, service state, active work, and action evidence before retry; duplicate requests cannot reinstall or flip pins repeatedly.
- [ ] Hermes can observe status and request an allowed typed promotion/control operation but receives no package-manager/root/SSH/release/GitHub credential or generic command surface.
- [ ] A canary rollout and documented rollback drill prove old-version recovery before production enablement.
- [ ] Tests cover active-work refusal, stale pin CAS, wrong tag/SHA, install failure, each validation failure, rollback success/failure, reboot/restart, duplicate requests, revocation, and secret canaries using injected installer/service/GitHub/git seams.
- [ ] Generated CLI/config/docs and `plugin/` mirror remain current; `npm run ci` passes.

## Non-goals

- Self-modifying Hermes skills/configuration or model-selected package sources.
- Changing the engine while any issue is active.
- Rewriting release tags or Releases.
- General host configuration management or distributed fleet rollout.
issues.title: feat(factory): coordinate exact-tag engine promotion, install, validation, and rollback
